# Notes for the report (observations to disclose; numbers to be regenerated by scripts at write-up time)
- Real data: SO-100 learned router rates 0.18 / 0.115 / 0.206 vs target 1/12 (router health not met on real data).
- Real data: all 3 Koch learned runs and 2 of 3 Koch Fixed runs stopped on the 45-min time cap (best epoch near the end).
- Real data: SO-100 entropy test compression 4.59 vs target 12: threshold fitted on only 5 validation episodes.
- Real data: learned boundaries come in long bursts (83–96% one-step gaps); seeds 0/1 burst at the grasp, seed 2 in transport (share 0).
- Entropy rule on Koch: 40% of boundaries within ±3 of a gripper event, 10.3x chance — strongest real-data aligner.
- Exploratory refractory router: sim F1 ±3 0.630 vs Fixed 0.594 (needs chance correction before any claim).
- Tiny GRU proxy (52k params, no chunking) has validation bits similar to the best learned model.
- Wording (Téo, 2026-10-30): verdicts stand as scored; H3 is reported as "significant but below threshold"
  (both datasets p < 0.001, ratios 1.89× and 1.77× vs the pre-registered 2×).
- Exploratory sections (chance-corrected F1, burst-merged F1, phase density, refractory window origin, real burst
  locations, entropy gripper-event finding) live in docs/EXPLORATORY.md, generated by scripts/exploratory_report.py.
  Re-run scripts/analyze.py exploratory + scripts/real_bursts.py + exploratory_report.py once sim_entropy_N5_s2 is done.

## H4 notes (2026-10-30, after scoring; numbers in runs/results_partB.json)
- Scored once with `analyze.py partB` after `partb_novelty.py` on partb_robochunk_N10_s0–2 / partb_flat_s0–2. Verdict as computed; nothing re-run.
- Several clean in-distribution candidates have *negative* gain (C2 near-duplicates, C3 new core episodes, C10 slow core),
  consistent across all 3 policy seeds, while exact duplicates (C1) are about neutral. Checked C2 for a data bug: same initial
  states as R, 199/200 equal lengths, mean |Δaction| matches the 0.05 noise, all demos successful — no bug found.
  Likely reading: with a fixed 20k updates, extra core-region data shifts the policy towards the core and costs broad-test
  generalisation. This makes the low-novelty end of the ranking negative rather than zero; the report must say so, because it
  contributes to ρ.
- Flat novelty gives nearly the same ρ as RoboChunk novelty; the chunked model adds little over an unchunked one here.

## H4 post-hoc diagnostics (requested 2026-10-30; NOT pre-registered; `scripts/h4_posthoc.py` → runs/results_partB_posthoc.json)
- Gains (95% CI): C1 -0.017 [-0.087, +0.055]; C2 -0.103 [-0.163, -0.042]; C3 -0.088 [-0.172, -0.010].
- BC budget is a fixed 20,000 gradient updates (batch 512), not epochs. Passes over the data: R 260, R ∪ C (200 episodes) 186.
- Success by broad-test subgroup (R / R∪C1 / R∪C2 / R∪C3): object in core square (n=50) 0.767 / 0.807 / 0.627 / 0.673; outside core (n=150) 0.327 / 0.291 / 0.236 / 0.240.
  C2 and C3 hurt *inside* the core region too, so the earlier reading (extra core data costs off-core generalisation) is not
  supported. Leading hypothesis: with fixed updates, new unique data lowers passes per sample and the policy under-fits;
  duplicates (C1) add no unique samples and stay neutral. Test queued after v2: `scripts/h4_matched_epochs.py` retrains
  R ∪ C1/C2/C3/C6 with updates scaled to R's passes (3 seeds), results in runs/results_partB_matched.json.
- Sensitivity, ρ over C4–C11 only (C1–C3 excluded, n = 8): 0.690 (p = 0.058).
- 95% CI for the pre-registered ρ = 0.782 (n = 11): Fisher z with Bonett–Wright SE [0.25, 0.95]; bootstrap over candidates [0.35, 0.95]. Both include values below the 0.6 threshold.
- **Matched-passes test result** (`scripts/h4_matched_epochs.py` → runs/results_partB_matched.json; updates scaled so R ∪ C
  gets R's ~260 passes, gain vs R at its original 20k updates): C1 +0.052 [-0.020, +0.123]; C2 +0.025 [-0.048, +0.098]; C3 +0.038 [-0.063, +0.153]; C6 +0.255 [+0.170, +0.335].
  C2 and C3 move from clearly negative to about zero (CIs include 0): the negative in-distribution gains were an artefact of
  the fixed-update BC budget, not of the data. C1 (no new information) rising too shows part of any gain is just more updates,
  so R itself was somewhat under-trained. Consequence for H4: the verdict stands as scored, but the negative low-novelty end
  that helped ρ came partly from this artefact. A fair re-test would re-run all 15 candidates (and R) at matched passes.
